en: Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed in clean, stagnant water, so emptying unused tires and containers prevents dengue fever.
Never chew apple seeds because they contain amygdalin, a compound that releases toxic cyanide when digested.
Drinking adequate water daily helps your kidneys filter blood waste and regulates your body temperature through sweating.
If a stray dog or cat bites you, wash the wound with soap and water immediately to prevent rabies.
The sap of the Euphorbia plant, commonly found in Philippine gardens, contains irritating chemicals that cause severe skin rashes.
Eating raw or undercooked freshwater fish can transmit parasitic liver flukes that severely damage your digestive system.
Getting nine to eleven hours of sleep each night allows your ten-year-old brain to consolidate memory and repair tissues.
Eating orange-fleshed sweet potatoes provides beta-carotene, which your body converts into vitamin A to maintain healthy eyesight.
When a honeybee stings you, it leaves a barbed stinger in your skin that continues pumping venom.
Properly burying or composting animal feces prevents parasite eggs from contaminating the soil and your root vegetables.
Applying sunscreen with an SPF of thirty or higher blocks ultraviolet B rays that cause sunburns.
Removing a tick within twenty-four hours prevents it from transmitting the bacteria that cause Lyme disease.
